A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Twilight and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched across renumbering and relocation, including v1 Appendix A and v3 Appendices A–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracy, A100 latency measurements, quantization analysis, and timing breakdowns in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds RULER evaluations, further baseline comparisons, sensitivity and kernel experiments, and CPU-offloading measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the conservative token selector, INT4 attention-weight estimation, binary-search top-p pruning, and final sparse attention. v3 elaborates head/group scheduling and quantization implementation, but does not establish that these replace a different v1 procedure; v1 already evaluates MHA and GQA models.

E1.justification: v3 adds RULER, including specialized non-retrieval CWE/FWE tests, alongside the retained Longbench, GSM8K, COQA, and PG-19 coverage. Appendix E also evaluates CPU-resident KV-cache offloading, introducing a distinct execution environment beyond v1's GPU-resident evaluation.

E2.justification: MagicPIG becomes an evaluated comparator on LLaMA-3.1 Longbench and RULER results. Appendix D adds StreamingLLM and SnapKV comparisons against DS-Twilight on Longchat Longbench; these methods were only discussed in v1. Quest, DS, and the existing dense-attention comparators remain.

E3.justification: The stated medium-context baseline budget changes from 64 to 128 tokens; this documents a protocol revision without independently establishing reruns. Added protocols include RULER at 16k–96k with 4%/8% baseline budgets, 4096-token token-dropping comparisons, threshold and kernel sweeps, and CPU-offloading latency tests.

E4.justification: v3 adds threshold-p sensitivity measurements (Figure 9), quantization-dependent SpGEMV latency (Figure 12), and padded versus head/group-variable-length attention comparisons (Figure 13). It also adds cumulative-weight and multilevel budget-dynamism examples. v1's quantization-accuracy and timing-breakdown analyses are retained and relocated, not removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Added averages and relative score changes remain point summaries rather than new uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial benchmark and diagnostic results, including offloading latencies of 8490.95 versus 527.77 microseconds for Quest versus Quest-Twi at 30k (Table 7). Medium-context comparator scores change under the revised budget, such as LLaMA-3.1 DS GSM8K flexible accuracy from 0.3806 to 0.6194; this is not a same-setting gain. Figure 7's maximum Quest-Twi/FA2 speedup changes from 15.4× to 15.8×. Longbench averages persist, but the final three task headers are reassigned without moving their values, preventing straightforward task-level performance comparisons.

T1.justification: The sparse-attention, oracle top-k, and oracle top-p definitions, attention-error bound, and hierarchical runtime model are retained. v3 specifies the Frobenius norm and makes selected-weight summations explicit, clarifying the existing argument without adding a substantively different theorem, proof, or formal result.

C1.justification: The central adaptive-pruning and near-lossless-accuracy claims remain. v3 foregrounds 1.4× acceleration over existing sparse attention, whereas v1 emphasizes larger gains over dense implementations. The conclusion revises the generic additional speedup from 2× to 1.4×, a limited refinement of the claimed benefit.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive discussion of the extra 1/8 KV-cache memory cost, why p is easier to tune, and the efficiency tradeoff of sharing selected tokens within GQA groups. Appendix F explicitly limits the favorable operating regime to cases where token loading dominates, acknowledges estimation overhead and architecture-integration difficulties, and identifies MLA support as future work.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-code URL and extensive implementation documentation: asynchronous loading, two-stage pipelining, FP16 dequantization, per-head scales and zeros, PTX conversion, bit packing, and flattened KV-cache scheduling. It also discloses DS configuration provenance and MagicPIG settings. Conversely, the accuracy setup no longer explicitly states v1's 8192-token initial selector budget for Longbench.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning beyond top-k methods, distinguishing MagicPIG's sampling, SampleAttention's prefill focus, and concurrent top-p work Tactic's distribution fitting. HShare, NSA, and MoBA are also added, alongside implementation-related references. This broadens the substantive comparison with prior and concurrent research, beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites explanatory prose throughout the introduction, method, and evaluation. It simplifies nested evaluation subsections, moves quantization-accuracy discussion into the implementation narrative, and reorganizes the appendix into six topical sections. The retained short-context experiments are consistently reframed as medium-context experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout. The architecture diagram is redrawn, attention-distribution plots change presentation and normalization, and several existing plots are restyled or relocated. v3 adds a main-text Longbench summary, RULER and supplementary comparison tables, and new sensitivity, budget-dynamism, and kernel figures. The detailed Longbench table also changes task headers.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation of the central adaptive-budget claim: v1 lacked threshold sensitivity and evaluated primarily against Quest and DS, while v3 adds those checks, non-top-k and token-dropping comparisons, and RULER coverage. Detailed implementation documentation and explicit memory, overhead, and GQA limitations also improve assessability. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, including the 15.8× Figure 7 maximum versus 15.4× in the conclusion and the unexplained Longbench column relabeling.
